candidates.lead: Wigan Council said it had listened and "struck the right balance" between supporting growth and creating jobs
candidates.evidence_text: Wigan council 'listening' as warehouse plans dropped - BBC News Image source, Joanna Allsop Image caption, Members of the Save Our Astley and Boothstown Greenbelt at a summer protest By Kevin Fitzpatrick North West Published 1 hour ago A consultation's due to end on Wigan Council's plan for future development, with four sites potentially earmarked for warehouses being removed. It follows an outcry from residents over the construction of huge warehouses close to homes near Astley. The local authority said it had listened and "struck the right balance between supporting economic growth and job creation". Greenbelt campaigners and opposition councillors claimed they had forced the council to act. Councils must put together a local plan which identifies sites for housing and business development every decade or so and Wigan is in the process of updating its own. In the version under consultation, it has said four sites would not be taken forward. They include to the north of M6 junction 26, Moss Industrial Estate extension, Bridgewater West in Astley, and West of Winwick Lane in Lowton. The site being described as Bridgewater West is known locally as Higher Green and more than half a million sqaure feet of employment space was to have been built. Joanna Allsop from the Save Our Astley and Boothstown Greenbelt lives nearby and said; "It was just unbelievable that anyone could suggest that it could be anything other than Greenbelt." She said they are still concerned about its future, adding: "What we want is long-lasting protection. We want them to say that it is Greenbelt, not try to say that it's Greybelt." 'Fiasco' The changes follow anger over the Astley warehouses which have led Mayor Bev Craig to question why modern industrial developments are being allowed so close to residential properties. Wigan Council's Labour leader, Councillor Nazia Rehman, said; "I would say some lessons have been learned, consultation will be proactive when it comes to communities and how they want their places changed and what type of developments they want to see in their area. "So we are working wherever we can to try to consult deeply when it comes to our communities." Leader of the opposition in Wigan, Reform UK Councillor Paul Watson said: "If there is one positive outcome from the Astley warehouse fiasco, it is that all the four additional commercial warehouse sites in the borough have been removed from the 2040 plan." The consultation ends at 17:00 BST on Wednesday 21st October 2026. candidates.title: Family's terror over mistaken HMO gang attack in Little Hulton
candidates.summary: The father says his family no no longer feel safe in their Salford house after it was targeted

candidates.lead: The father says his family no no longer feel safe in their Salford house after it was targeted
candidates.evidence_text: Family's terror over mistaken HMO gang attack in Little Hulton - BBC News Image source, MEN Image caption, The father said he does not feel safe in his Salford home after it was mistakenly attacked By Charlotte Hall Local Democracy Reporting Service Published 20 October 2026 A father has told of his family's terror after their home was mistakenly attacked by a balaclava-wearing gang opposed to Houses of Multiple Occupancy (HMOs). Black graffiti reading: "No HMOs, No, No" was daubed over the house in Little Hulton, Salford, and a brick was smashed threw through their living room window on 13 October. The family's two sons, aged four and two, were asleep upstairs at the time. Their father said: "We want to get out of here. It feels unsafe." Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said there had been 25 attacks across Salford on houses thought to be HMOs since 5 October with most "racially or religiously motivated". The Local Democracy Reporting Service (LDRS) said there were fears the attacks on HMOs suspected of housing migrants had been fuelled by far-right influencers who had posted videos of the homes on social media. Salford City Council's planning lead Mike McCusker said: "There's been a set-up that's led to this. "Filming outside possible HMOs, coupled with the national rhetoric about that you see from far right political groups on a national level about HMO." The LDRS said a flat housing a group of young Sudanese refugees who fled genocide has been attacked. But others houses targeted have included homes of NHS nurses and care workers. Cars and homes have been vandalised and a pig's severed head was left outside one home on 13 October. On the same night, the father-of-two's home was bricked as he sat in his living room. The man, who did not want to be named, said: "We've lived here for a year and had no issues, until now. "The police say they're targeting HMOs, but this isn't a HMO. "It's me and my wife, we have two small kids." Image source, LDRS Image caption, A brick was thrown through the family's home Ch Insp Lee Gridley, said: "This spate of offending is being treated with the seriousness it deserves. "No one should be made to feel unsafe in their own home and it's not something that will be tolerated in Salford, or anywhere in Greater Manchester." Image source, MEN Image caption, There are fears the violence has been fuelled by far-right influencers on social media Two men, aged 39 and 46, have been arrested on suspicion of conspiracy to commit criminal damage over the attacks. However police fear children are being used to carry out the attacks. A 13-year-old boy was arrested last week. Det Ch Insp Helen Bagnall, said: "We believe this offending is linked to the criminal exploitation of children, with vulnerable young people being encouraged by others to commit acts of criminal damage on their behalf. candidates.lead: One man says he is "like a zombie" due to not being able to sleep through lorries driving past his house
candidates.evidence_text: 'M67 motorway closures mean I can't sleep at night' - BBC News Image caption, Francoise Sullivan said additional traffic noise caused by lorries being diverted from the M67 was keeping her and her husband awake at night By Richard Stead North West Published 20 October 2026 A couple have said they cannot sleep due to traffic being diverted past their home at night during long-running motorway improvements. The M67 has been closed in both directions on weeknights between 20:00 and 06:00 since July and lorries and cars will continue to be diverted onto Mottram Road, in Godley, Tameside, until December. Francoise Sullivan, who has lived on the road since 1987, said: "It's a nightmare - we just can't sleep from the noise and the vibrations. We've been given some medication but it doesn't really help because the house shakes, the bed shakes and we worry what it's doing to our house." National Highways said it "understands" the impact roadworks can have on local people. Image caption, Work is taking place at the M67 Junction 4 roundabout as part of the Mottram bypass scheme Image caption, John Sullivan said HGVs should be directed away from Mottram Road when the M67 is closed John Sullivan said: "You can't relax in your own home and you can't sleep at night because you're waiting for the next lorry." The 75-year-old former Tameside mayor added: "I'm like a zombie in the daytime and it's an absolutely dreadful, dreadful way to have to live." On one night when the M67 was closed, the couple say they counted 758 HGVs and 4,609 cars passing their home in Godley between 20:00 and 06:00. The couple have also urged Tameside Council to resurface Mottram Road and impose a reduced speed limit to minimise noise. The regular closure of the M67 is part of the A57 Link Roads scheme, designed to take traffic travelling between Manchester and Sheffield away from the village of Mottram in Longdendale. Construction of the bypass is set to be completed during the winter of 2028-29. Image source, John Sullivan Image caption, Traffic is being diverted onto Mottram Road during the M67 overnight closures Karen Cliffe, National Highways' programme manager, said: "We understand the impact roadworks can have and we've met with Mr and Mrs Sullivan to explain our approach. "We carefully planned this work to minimise disruption and, in partnership with Tameside Council, determined that the A57 is an appropriate diversion route because it accepts all forms of motorway traffic, including HGVs." A council spokesperson said: "We appreciate the disturbance that increased traffic levels, particularly HGV movements, may be causing to residents along the diversion route. "Classified routes like Mottram Road are designed to convey the majority of traffic through the borough and we are obliged to agree to the diversion but we're liaising with National Highways to look at how they can mitigate the impact on local residents." Image caption, Reform UK councillor Allan Hopwood said the overnight closures were causing too much disruption The work on the A57 Link Roads scheme has meant the remodelling of the roundabout at the end of the M67 in Mottram. Farmer Allan Hopwood, who lives nearby and is the leader of Reform UK on Tameside Council, said: "It's been an absolute disaster from start to finish because it's meant extra traffic through Hattersley and through the centre of Mottram. "If I want to cross the roundabout, I have to make a phone call to get a chaperone who can escort me across the site but I've sometimes had to wait 45 minutes for somebody to let me in to my own land." evidence_packet.evidence_text: A couple have said they cannot sleep due to traffic being diverted past their home at night during long-running motorway improvements The M67 has been closed in both directions on weeknights between 20:00 and 06:00 since July and lorries and cars will continue to be diverted onto Mottram Road, in Godley, Tameside, until December Francoise Sullivan, who has lived on the road since 1987, said: "It's a nightmare - we just can't sleep from the noise and the vibrations. We've been given some medication but it doesn't really help because the house shakes, the bed shakes and we worry what it's doing to our hous National Highways said it "understands" the impact roadworks can have on local people John Sullivan said: "You can't relax in your own home and you can't sleep at night because you're waiting for the next lorry." The 75-year-old former Tameside mayor added: "I'm like a zombie in the daytime and it's an absolutely dreadful, dreadful way to have to live."

candidates.summary: The project has risen from £330m to almost £525m, with reopening planned for spring 2027

candidates.practical_angle: Сверить, остаётся ли история актуальной для сегодняшнего дня перед публикацией.
candidates.lead: The project has risen from £330m to almost £525m, with reopening planned for spring 2027
candidates.evidence_text: Manchester Town Hall £525m budget will not rise, leader says - BBC News Image caption, Restoration work at Manchester Town Hall was initially expected to be finished in 2024 By Naj Modak , Haider Saleem , North West and Juliet Phillips , Reporting from Manchester Published 20 October 2026 The leader of Manchester City Council has said there will be no extra cash for restoring the city's historic Town Hall. The project's original budget was £330m but has since risen to almost £525m, following delays and unexpected problems during the restoration. Garry Bridges said the project was now coming in on its revised budget and there would be "no more increases". The Grade I-listed Victorian building closed in 2018 for the work, which was initially expected to be completed by 2024. It is now due to reopen to the public in spring 2027. Image caption, The restoration has involved painstaking work to preserve the building's historic features Bridges described the work as the largest heritage restoration project in the country and said the coronavirus pandemic, inflation and even nesting birds on the roof had contributed to delays and rising costs. "This is an enormous investment by the people of Manchester themselves into a building that they own and is part of their history," he said. "There's been a lot of things that have made additional cost but we're really pleased to say that after we've revised the budget, it is now coming in on budget and there won't be any more increases." Image caption, Councillor Garry Bridges Workers have faced a number of challenges during the restoration, including unexpected discoveries beneath the floors. One member of the restoration team said large amounts of heavily compacted sawdust had been found beneath a former dance floor. He suggested the material might have been installed to reduce noise travelling to rooms below when the floor was replaced in the 1960s. The sawdust had to be broken out by hand and removed from the building, rather than being vacuumed up. "It took us 18 weeks just to remove the sawdust," he said. Other discoveries beneath the floors meant the underfloor heating system had to be redesigned. Image caption, A member of the restoration team explains the painstaking work carried out on the Town Hall's historic windows The restoration has also involved painstaking work on the building's historic lighting, including six large ceiling lights originally designed for gas lighting. A member of the team said some wall lights had been stripped of several layers of paint, revealing original designs which were then recreated using matching colours. Elsewhere, about 160,000 roof tiles have been replaced, while work on the historic windows has involved removing and reinstalling individual panes of glass. Opening to the public Bridges said the restored Town Hall would offer visitors access to parts of the building which many people had never seen before. "The big thing about this reopening is it will be open to the public in a way that it never has been before," he said. "Buildings like this were often built just as much to keep people out as to invite people in and were a statement about the power of the people that held office within them." He said a new reception area and visitor experience would tell the story of the building, the city and its civic history. New lifts have been installed to make all floors accessible, while visitors will be able to enter through accessible entrances. However, some areas, including those used by coroners, registrars and senior council officials, will remain closed to visitors. Bridges said the reopening would be marked by a programme of events throughout 2027, culminating in celebrations of the building's 150th anniversary in September. "There will be many opportunities for people to come and visit and to come and celebrate throughout that whole year," he said. But, he said, the reopening would take place over a period of time, with people able to enter the building in spring before it was fully staffed and occupied. candidates.evidence_text: North West health correspondent Published 1 hour ago Younger adults living in the north of England are 42% more likely to die than their counterparts in the South, according to new research A study by academics in Manchester and Liverpool found people in the North aged 25 to 49 faced a significantly higher risk of death than people of the same age living in southern England Researchers said deprivation was a major factor behind the gap and called for urgent action to tackle inequalities The Department of Health and Social Care said it was determined to reduce health inequalities and close the divide The research, by the University of Manchester, the University of Liverpool and Health Equity North, analysed deaths between 1981 and 2024 It found that while death rates fell overall, the gap between younger adults in the north and south more than tripled. Overall, people aged 25 to 49 in the north had a 42% higher death rate, compared with 13% in 1981

candidates.evidence_text: Film director Danny Boyle said his new film about the rise of The Sun newspaper does not shy away from its coverage of the Hillsborough disaster The Oscar-winning director from Bury said the 1989 headline 'The Truth', which falsely blamed Liverpool fans for the tragedy, was "one of the darkest days in publishing history" Boyle made the comments at a screening of Ink in Manchester ahead of the film's release next year The film, due to stream on Netflix next year, stars Guy Pearce as media mogul Rupert Murdoch, Jack O'Connell as editor Larry Lamb and Claire Foy as a reporter Despite what he described as the "disgrace of Hillsborough", Boyle said he took on the project because he saw parallels between the newspaper's rise and today's "clickbait world", adding that Fleet Street during that era was a "riveting piece of British history" Speaking to BBC North West Tonight , Boyle said the film "doesn't shy away" from The Sun's coverage of the Hillsborough disaster

candidates.evidence_text: Salford Number of firefighters attacked around bonfire night on the rise in Salford The attacks are becoming more frequent, alongside firework-related antisocial behaviour. Add to preferred sources News Charlotte Hall Local Democracy Reporter 20:01, 2 Attacks on firefighters and firework-related antisocial behaviour (ASB) are on the rise in Salford as the council and police tackle crime linked to the autumn period, a report has found Last year, the city saw an 18 per cent increase in fire crew being verbally threatened or assaulted while trying to do their jobs on famously busy nights like Halloween and Bonfire night. A total of 20 incidents were reported in 2025 Firework-related antisocial behaviour was also found to have risen slightly, according to a report on Operation Treacle, a Greater Manchester-wide mission to proactively deal with spikes in ASB on November 5. There were a total of 1,020 occurrences, up by two percent from 2024 The report, which was presented at a scrutiny panel at the town hall on Monday, September 18, also found a total of 935 fires were set deliberately during the October to November period. Almost 200 of these were classed as ‘primary fires’ – which are blazes that cause harm to peo View 2 Images The bonfire night period is one of the busiest times for fire crew. (Image: Manchester Evening News)

candidates.evidence_text: Trafford Housing plan to be taken forward for Altrincham's Planet Ice site in 'once-in-a-generation' opportunity More than 100 homes could be built on the site Add to preferred sources Comments News Hannah Richardson 17:33, 20 Oct 2026 View 2 Images P New homes should be built on Altrincham’s Planet Ice site, town hall bosses have said Trafford councillors weighed up two competing visions for land off Oakfield Road , in the town, at its cabinet meeting last night. The first proposal was for a residential-led scheme, with a council spokeswoman saying more than 100 homes could be built there Option two would have seen a retail-led approach taken, with this expected to include a large food store or supermarket. The land, near Altrincham Interchange, currently comprises the Planet Ice ice rink and around 320 parking spaces Development there has stalled since 2007, despite a series of development proposals coming forward. These have included offices, a hotel, shops, a hospital, a bowling alley and a leisure centre None of the schemes ever materialised, however, and developer Nikal went into administration in 2023. Trafford council decided to acquire the site in 2024, paying a little more than £2m for it

candidates.evidence_text: Salford Another building bulldozed, but it could mark the beginning of something major in Salford The two-storey building has been vacant since September Add to preferred sources News Charlotte Hall Local Democracy Reporter 06:11, 21 Oct 2026 View 2 I An application to demolish a vacant business site in Salford could mark the beginning of a major new development in Ordsall Landowners Tokenhouse Pensions Trust have submitted a prior notification of proposed demolition for Walker House on King William Street. The two-storey redbrick building is near the Anchorage tram stop and a stones’ throw from a number of large housing developments such as Clay S Last home to a commercial business, the building has been vacant since September 4, 2026, according to the landowners In an application submitted to the council, a representative explained the building is being bulldozed as part of plans to redevelop the land – currently in the middle of an industrial business park – into a large-scale residential project View 2 Images The two-storey building is already in the shadow of several larger housing develpments. (Image: Copyright Unknown)

candidates.evidence_text: Heaton Norris Residents terrified and windows smashed as quiet Stockport street becomes latest to fall victim to vile 'HMO' attacks The owners said they plan to house young professionals there, not asylum seekers, and criticised rumours circulating on People living in a Stockport suburb say they have been left 'terrified' after the windows of a terraced house were smashed in overnight Last week, two properties in Heaton Norris just outside Stockport town centre were targeted with anti-HMO graffiti . The Manchester Evening News understands one of the properties was targeted again shortly after 3am on October 20, when windows smashed The vandalism and criminal damage follows similar incidents in Salford where suspected houses of multiple occupation, commonly referred to as HMOs, were targeted. A police investigation is ongoing Neither of the properties in Heaton Norris are currently used as HMOs, despite claims on social media. One is understood to be for sale while the owners of the property where the windows were smashed are asking Stockport council for permission to convert it into an eight bedroom HMOs are properties where at least three tenants live there forming more than one household. They also share toilet, bathroom or kitchen facilities with the other tenants

candidates.evidence_text: Salford Number of firefighters attacked around bonfire night on the rise in Salford The attacks are becoming more frequent, alongside firework-related antisocial behaviour. Add to preferred sources News Charlotte Hall Local Democracy Reporter 20:01, 2 Attacks on firefighters and firework-related antisocial behaviour (ASB) are on the rise in Salford as the council and police tackle crime linked to the autumn period, a report has found Last year, the city saw an 18 per cent increase in fire crew being verbally threatened or assaulted while trying to do their jobs on famously busy nights like Halloween and Bonfire night. A total of 20 incidents were reported in 2025 Firework-related antisocial behaviour was also found to have risen slightly, according to a report on Operation Treacle, a Greater Manchester-wide mission to proactively deal with spikes in ASB on November 5. There were a total of 1,020 occurrences, up by two percent from 2024 The report, which was presented at a scrutiny panel at the town hall on Monday, September 18, also found a total of 935 fires were set deliberately during the October to November period. Almost 200 of these were classed as ‘primary fires’ – which are blazes that cause harm to peo View 2 Images The bonfire night period is one of the busiest times for fire crew. (Image: Manchester Evening News)

candidates.evidence_text: Courts Murder accused led police on pursuit day after hitting headteacher and dragging him underneath car, trial hears Simon Richardson, 35, denies murdering 56-year-old Michael Mullins Add to preferred sources News Amy Walker Court reporter 18:39, 20 A murder trial has heard how a driver led police on a pursuit the day after he allegedly struck Stretford Grammar headteacher Michael Mullins as he cycled home from work, before dragging him underneath his car for over a mile Simon Richardson, 35, is alleged to have struck Michael Mullins as he pedalled home from work at Stretford Grammar School, on April 20. Prosecutors allege that Mr Richardson did not stop and 'put his foot down', dragging 56-year-old Mr Mullins along the road for 2.2km - or 1.3 mi Earlier in the trial, witnesses described seeing the Volvo ‘absolutely tanking it’ towards the junction of Dunham Road and Warburton Lane. Mr Richardson denies murder, an alternate offence of manslaughter and dangerous driving, and is on trial at Manchester's Minshull Street Crow On day six of the trial, jurors heard evidence about an alleged course of dangerous driving undertaken by Mr Richardson on the morning of April 21, this year View 3 Images Michael Mullins (Image: Manchester Evening News)

candidates.evidence_text: Moss Side 'Loving' grandmother at centre of Moss Side murder investigation named "Yvonne was a much-loved mum, Nana, sister and auntie, known for her caring heart, strength and kindness," said her heartbroken family Add to preferred sources News Ashli The 'much-loved' grandmother who was tragically found dead in her Moss Side home has been named. Emergency services rushed to the area following reports of a disturbance at a property on Crondall Street just before 1.30pm on Monday (October 19) Tragically, the body of a woman was found. The victim has been named by her family as, Yvonne Kemp. A 26-year-old woman has been arrested on suspicion of murder and has been detained under the Mental Health Act In a heartfelt tribute to Yvonne, her family said: “Yvonne was a much-loved mum, Nana, sister and auntie, known for her caring heart, strength and kindness “She was the kind of person who would do anything for anyone, always putting others before herself “She leaves behind a family who love her dearly and memories that will be cherished forever

candidates.lead: Trafford Housing plan to be taken forward for Altrincham's Planet Ice site in 'once-in-a-generation' opportunity More than 100 homes could be built on the site Add to preferred sources Comments News Hannah Richardson 17:33, 20 Oct 2026 View 2 Images P New homes should be built on
candidates.evidence_text: Trafford Housing plan to be taken forward for Altrincham's Planet Ice site in 'once-in-a-generation' opportunity More than 100 homes could be built on the site Add to preferred sources Comments News Hannah Richardson 17:33, 20 Oct 2026 View 2 Images P New homes should be built on Altrincham’s Planet Ice site, town hall bosses have said Trafford councillors weighed up two competing visions for land off Oakfield Road , in the town, at its cabinet meeting last night. The first proposal was for a residential-led scheme, with a council spokeswoman saying more than 100 homes could be built there Option two would have seen a retail-led approach taken, with this expected to include a large food store or supermarket. The land, near Altrincham Interchange, currently comprises the Planet Ice ice rink and around 320 parking spaces Development there has stalled since 2007, despite a series of development proposals coming forward. These have included offices, a hotel, shops, a hospital, a bowling alley and a leisure centre None of the schemes ever materialised, however, and developer Nikal went into administration in 2023. Trafford council decided to acquire the site in 2024, paying a little more than £2m for it

candidates.evidence_text: Courts Woman's bizarre courtroom outburst as she and husband are jailed for £1.1m drug conspiracy Guixiang Liu and Yanfeng He concealed cannabis and MDMA in picture frames and cushion covers Add to preferred sources Comments News Greta Simpson Senior A woman who helped arrange the import and export of more than £1 million worth of drugs shouted ‘WHERE IS THE MONEY’ at barristers as she and her husband were jailed at Minshull Street Crown Court today (October 20) Guixiang Liu and her husband Yanfeng He used cushion covers, speakers and picture frames to conceal shipments of MDMA and cannabis, the court heard These were then prepared for shipment as far as the Solomon Islands, Argentina and Australia, in what was described as a ‘sophisticated, organised, sustained’ international drug trafficking operation taking place between June and December 2019 Liu and He, both 48 and of Kenmere Grove in Moston , were convicted of conspiring to fraudulently evade prohibition by importing MDMA and cannabis - and conspiracy to supply the same - at trial earlier this year The parcels were intercepted by Border Force officers, prompting an NCA investigation which uncovered parcels of drugs, labelled with fake names, being sent around the world facilitated through Chinese messaging app WeChat

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Woman's bizarre courtroom outburst as she and husband are jailed for £1.1m drug conspiracy Guixiang Liu and Yanfeng He concealed cannabis and MDMA in picture frames and cushion covers Add to preferred sources Comments News Greta Simpson Senior A woman who helped arrange the import and export of more than £1 million worth of drugs shouted ‘WHERE IS THE MONEY’ at barristers as she and her husband were jailed at Minshull Street Crown Court today (October 20) Guixiang Liu and her husband Yanfeng He used cushion covers, speakers and picture frames to conceal shipments of MDMA and cannabis, the court heard These were then prepared for shipment as far as the Solomon Islands, Argentina and Australia, in what was described as a ‘sophisticated, organised, sustained’ international drug trafficking operation taking place between June and December 2019 Liu and He, both 48 and of Kenmere Grove in Moston , were convicted of conspiring to fraudulently evade prohibition by importing MDMA and cannabis - and conspiracy to supply the same - at trial earlier this year The parcels were intercepted by Border Force officers, prompting an NCA investigation which uncovered parcels of drugs, labelled with fake names, being sent around the world facilitated through Chinese messaging app WeChat

candidates.evidence_text: Heaton Norris Residents terrified and windows smashed as quiet Stockport street becomes latest to fall victim to vile 'HMO' attacks The owners said they plan to house young professionals there, not asylum seekers, and criticised rumours circulating on People living in a Stockport suburb say they have been left 'terrified' after the windows of a terraced house were smashed in overnight Last week, two properties in Heaton Norris just outside Stockport town centre were targeted with anti-HMO graffiti . The Manchester Evening News understands one of the properties was targeted again shortly after 3am on October 20, when windows smashed The vandalism and criminal damage follows similar incidents in Salford where suspected houses of multiple occupation, commonly referred to as HMOs, were targeted. A police investigation is ongoing Neither of the properties in Heaton Norris are currently used as HMOs, despite claims on social media. One is understood to be for sale while the owners of the property where the windows were smashed are asking Stockport council for permission to convert it into an eight bedroom HMOs are properties where at least three tenants live there forming more than one household. They also share toilet, bathroom or kitchen facilities with the other tenants

She ran in my room just screaming and screaming' WARNING CONTAINS GRAPHIC IMAGES Add to preferred sources News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 06: A 10-year-girl was rushed to hospital while 'screaming in pain' when her glitter phone case cracked - leaking fluid all over her stomach - her mother has said Nikita Bourne's daughter Soraya was treated for severe chemical burns following the terrifying incident at home in Old Trafford earlier this month. She says she has been left with large burn marks across her belly from the unknown chemical At the moment, it is not known if there will be any long-term scarring. Ms Bourne said Soraya was playing on her phone in her bedroom when the case cracked and leaked onto her midriff. She added: "It was just awful. She ran in my room just screaming and screaming "At first she was in so much pain she couldn't get her words out. She was just saying 'the phone, the phone'. I was terrified. I didn't know what was going on. Then I looked at the phone and there was just a little crack in it. I realised it was a chemical burn." candidates.evidence_text: Wigan There are plans for a 37-bed HMO in Leigh, but the council has 'significant concerns' The proposed 'mixed use' conversion has led to concerns about over-concentration of such properties Add to preferred sources Comments News Chris Gee Local demo Housing bosses in Wigan have expressed ‘significant concerns’ about plans for a ‘flexible’ HMO and hotel for up to 48 people in Leigh. Oldham-based Spencer Reid Ltd has submitted proposals for three adjacent buildings in Leigh town centre The application for buildings on Railway Road seeks approval to convert the properties into a mixed hotel and HMO building with 39 bedrooms with a capacity for 48 people The applicant said the ‘mixed use’ element of the application would allow hotel stays for tourists and business visitors ‘in the usual manner’ A response to the application from the council’s housing enabling team has been published by the authority The report said ‘we do have significant concerns regarding this HMO’

candidates.evidence_text: Wigan Wigan man rumbled by locals after stealing stones worth £7,000 from historic sites A series of thefts of coping stones from historic boundary walls in West Lancashire took place over several months last year Add to preferred sources News Amy Fen Police have revealed how members of the public helped to trace the Wigan thief who stole stones from historic locations in West Lancashire Last year, a string of thefts occurred over several months involving the removal of coping stones from boundary walls in the Rufford area of West Lancashire With officers finding the case "particularly challenging" due to the isolated locations of the crimes, local residents intervened and placed "discreet tracking devices" in stones they suspected would be targeted On the evening of October 25 last year, stones were taken from a location. Among them was one which had been equipped with a tracking device, reports Lancs Live The stone's location was then given to officers, who traced it to the home address of Craig Barker in Wigan

candidates.evidence_text: Courts Woman's bizarre courtroom outburst as she and husband are jailed for £1.1m drug conspiracy Guixiang Liu and Yanfeng He concealed cannabis and MDMA in picture frames and cushion covers Add to preferred sources Comments News Greta Simpson Senior A woman who helped arrange the import and export of more than £1 million worth of drugs shouted ‘WHERE IS THE MONEY’ at barristers as she and her husband were jailed at Minshull Street Crown Court today (October 20) Guixiang Liu and her husband Yanfeng He used cushion covers, speakers and picture frames to conceal shipments of MDMA and cannabis, the court heard These were then prepared for shipment as far as the Solomon Islands, Argentina and Australia, in what was described as a ‘sophisticated, organised, sustained’ international drug trafficking operation taking place between June and December 2019 Liu and He, both 48 and of Kenmere Grove in Moston , were convicted of conspiring to fraudulently evade prohibition by importing MDMA and cannabis - and conspiracy to supply the same - at trial earlier this year The parcels were intercepted by Border Force officers, prompting an NCA investigation which uncovered parcels of drugs, labelled with fake names, being sent around the world facilitated through Chinese messaging app WeChat

candidates.evidence_text: Salford Number of firefighters attacked around bonfire night on the rise in Salford The attacks are becoming more frequent, alongside firework-related antisocial behaviour. Add to preferred sources News Charlotte Hall Local Democracy Reporter 20:01, 2 Attacks on firefighters and firework-related antisocial behaviour (ASB) are on the rise in Salford as the council and police tackle crime linked to the autumn period, a report has found Last year, the city saw an 18 per cent increase in fire crew being verbally threatened or assaulted while trying to do their jobs on famously busy nights like Halloween and Bonfire night. A total of 20 incidents were reported in 2025 Firework-related antisocial behaviour was also found to have risen slightly, according to a report on Operation Treacle, a Greater Manchester-wide mission to proactively deal with spikes in ASB on November 5. There were a total of 1,020 occurrences, up by two percent from 2024 The report, which was presented at a scrutiny panel at the town hall on Monday, September 18, also found a total of 935 fires were set deliberately during the October to November period. Almost 200 of these were classed as ‘primary fires’ – which are blazes that cause harm to peo View 2 Images The bonfire night period is one of the busiest times for fire crew. (Image: Manchester Evening News)

Emergency services rushed to the area following reports of a disturbance at a property on Crondall Street just before 1.30pm on Monday (October 19) Tragically, the body of a woman was found. The victim has been named by her family as, Yvonne Kemp. A 26-year-old woman has been arrested on suspicion of murder and has been detained under the Mental Health Act In a heartfelt tribute to Yvonne, her family said: “Yvonne was a much-loved mum, Nana, sister and auntie, known for her caring heart, strength and kindness “She was the kind of person who would do anything for anyone, always putting others before herself “She leaves behind a family who love her dearly and memories that will be cherished forever

candidates.evidence_text: Trafford Housing plan to be taken forward for Altrincham's Planet Ice site in 'once-in-a-generation' opportunity More than 100 homes could be built on the site Add to preferred sources Comments News Hannah Richardson 17:33, 20 Oct 2026 View 2 Images P New homes should be built on Altrincham’s Planet Ice site, town hall bosses have said Trafford councillors weighed up two competing visions for land off Oakfield Road , in the town, at its cabinet meeting last night. The first proposal was for a residential-led scheme, with a council spokeswoman saying more than 100 homes could be built there Option two would have seen a retail-led approach taken, with this expected to include a large food store or supermarket. The land, near Altrincham Interchange, currently comprises the Planet Ice ice rink and around 320 parking spaces Development there has stalled since 2007, despite a series of development proposals coming forward. These have included offices, a hotel, shops, a hospital, a bowling alley and a leisure centre None of the schemes ever materialised, however, and developer Nikal went into administration in 2023. Trafford council decided to acquire the site in 2024, paying a little more than £2m for it

The first proposal was for a residential-led scheme, with a council spokeswoman saying more than 100 homes could be built there Option two would have seen a retail-led approach taken, with this expected to include a large food store or supermarket. The land, near Altrincham Interchange, currently comprises the Planet Ice ice rink and around 320 parking spaces Development there has stalled since 2007, despite a series of development proposals coming forward. These have included offices, a hotel, shops, a hospital, a bowling alley and a leisure centre None of the schemes ever materialised, however, and developer Nikal went into administration in 2023. Trafford council decided to acquire the site in 2024, paying a little more than £2m for it

Amar Manzoor raped and assaulted one woman; stalked another, causing her 'serious alarm and distress'; and raped and attacked a third While in police custody following his arrest on suspicion of strangulation, the 42-year-old attempted to contact one of the women, Greater Manchester Police said Manzoor, from Bolton, 'tried to coerce her to withdraw her statement and also attempted to force her to create false contact details in an effort to avoid detection,' the force added A jury convicted him of three counts of rape; two counts of controlling and coercive behaviour; three counts of assault; two counts of perverting the course of justice; one count of non-fatal strangulation; and one count of stalking He was jailed for 22 years by a judge at Bolton Crown Court on Monday (October 19). In a statement, one of Manzoor's victims said: "I have had to change so much in order to protect myself. So much so that I don't even recognise myself anymore."

Trains between the two stations were cancelled, delayed or revised Operators affected included Northern and TransPennine Express. Lines were reopened at around 9.30am, but passengers were warned of disruption continuing into the afternoon National Rail said: "All lines have now reopened following an earlier failure of the electricity supply in the Preston area. Trains between Preston and Bolton may continue to be cancelled, revised or delayed by up to 45 minutes. Disruption is expected until 15:00." Northern said all lines were blocked between Preston and Bolton, with the route between Millom/Barrow-in-Furness/Windermere/Blackpool North and Manchester Airport affected. TransPennine Express said routes between Manchester Airport and Glasgow Central and Manchester Airport and Network Rail, who run Manchester Piccadilly station, said in a post on X: "Sorry to passengers impacted by the damage to the overhead power lines near Preston. Lines were reopened at around 9.30am, but passengers were warned of disruption continuing into the afternoon National Rail said: "All lines have now reopened following an earlier failure of the electricity supply in the Preston area. Trains between Preston and Bolton may continue to be cancelled, revised or delayed by up to 45 minutes. Disruption is expected until 15:00." Northern said all lines were blocked between Preston and Bolton, with the route between Millom/Barrow-in-Furness/Windermere/Blackpool North and Manchester Airport affected. TransPennine Express said routes between Manchester Airport and Glasgow Central and Manchester Airport and Network Rail, who run Manchester Piccadilly station, said in a post on X: "Sorry to passengers impacted by the damage to the overhead power lines near Preston. candidates.evidence_text: Wednesday 14 October 2026 at 10:33am Kirith Entwistle, the Labour MP for Bolton North East, has said she found the current court system "triggering" and had to watch her abuser "stare at her". Credit: UK Parliament A Labour MP has revealed that she is a victim of domestic abuse - Speaking in the Commons on October 13, Kirith Entwistle, who represents Bolton North East, described her experience of the current court system as "triggering", adding that she had to watch her abuser "stare at her" during a recent video hearing Ms Entwistle told her fellow MPs that she believes special measures - where victims are given protection or assistance in court - should be the standard in cases involving domestic abuse Examples of these measures could include screens, the ability to give evidence through a live link, or witnesses being able to be accompanied when giving evidence Measures to protect victims are included in the Courts and Tribunals Bill, which is currently going through Parliament Speaking during a debate on the bill, Ms Entwistle said: "It doesn’t matter how many times somebody tells me that they understand what I’m going through, or they acknowledge what I’ve been through, they really don’t unless they have lived it themselves or know somebody who has."

Credit: 499883 A man who murdered a mother and four of her children in a firebomb attack had been arrested and released by police despite Zak Bolland, 26, walked free from a police station after giving a 12-minute ‘no comment’ interview for breaking the windows of the home of Michelle Pearson, 37, and her young family in Jackson Street in Walkden, Greater Manchester on November 26 2017 Bolland’s previous convictions and suspended jail sentence he was serving at the time had not been checked by police and he was told he would be ‘NFA’d’ – no further action taken against him over the windows attack, Bolton Coroner’s Court heard Thirteen days later, in the dead of night on December 11 2017, he smashed Ms Pearson’s windows again and tossed in a petrol bomb which “exploded” near the stairs, blocking the only exit to the ground floor and trapping the victims upstairs Demi Pearson, 15, her brother Brandon, eight, and sisters Lacie, seven, and Lia, three, all died in the blaze Ms Pearson suffered 68% burns to her body and “clung on to life” until she died, 20 months after the attack on August 25 2019

candidates.lead: Living in Manchester means accepting that rain is practically a permanent fixture on your calendar.
candidates.evidence_text: Living in Manchester means accepting that rain is practically a permanent fixture on your calendar. That relentless North West damp air has an annoying habit of turning a fresh, polished morning style into a frizzy mess before you even manage to reach the tram stop. Navigating co Hair naturally swells when it absorbs excess moisture from humid air, causing the outer cuticle layer to lift and create instant frizz. Keeping your strands properly hydrated while you are still in the shower stops them from seeking out and soaking up that damp outdoor air later Hair is at its most fragile state when wet because the internal structural bonds temporarily stretch. Yanking a standard comb or an aggressive paddle brush through damp strands creates micro-breakage that eventually shows up as frayed split ends a few weeks down the line. Adoptin Rough towel drying destroys smooth hair texture faster than almost anything else in your routine. Vigorously rubbing your head with a heavy bath towel roughens the cuticle layer instantly and triggers immediate frizz before you even reach for a hairdryer. A much smarter approach Whenever local humidity levels spike, using heat styling tools without proper pre-styling protection almost guarantees dull, damaged ends. Layering a lightweight leave-in conditioner or a thermal spray shields your hair before you blow-dry. Plenty of beauty enthusiasts regularly Rethinking how you treat damp hair makes an incredible difference in how well your style holds up outdoors. A few small, intentional tweaks to your daily routine will keep your hair looking healthy, smooth, and effortless every day of the week

Some people find strength in a walking group, a community café or a peer support network, while others need specialist help for issues such as addiction, which can sit alongside anxiety Loneliness can affect anyone, including young adults, new parents, carers, older people and those who have recently moved to the area. Community centres, libraries, sports clubs, allotment groups and local arts projects can help people form meaningful relationships. Even small ge Greater Manchester has many diverse communities, and support should be culturally sensitive and accessible. This means providing information in different languages, recognising different family structures, and working with trusted local leaders who understand the needs of their n Stigma remains one of the biggest barriers to getting support. People don’t always describe themselves as “depressed” or “anxious”; they may say they are exhausted, overwhelmed, angry, numb or unable to cope. Listening without rushing to offer solutions can make a real difference

She’s wearing Musera, which looks to be Manchester’s friendliest, chicest new clothing label — launched in 2024 from an From this Newton Street office, a band of young designers turn out a stream of trend pieces: low-rise trousers and asymmetric tops, distressed knitwear and leopard-print flares, western fringed jumpers and A-level prom gowns. Their Instagram bio lauds the brand as “Est. MCR.” Over a million people watched the staff dancing around their Northern Quarter office to Whigfield’s Saturday Night on TikTok. More still tuned in to a video showing them kitted out in Musera for Drake’s performance at Co-op Live last year. And who knows how many have sidestepped “Be a muse in your own era,” goes their slogan; presumably also the source of their similarly recondite name. Their Instagram captions are a list of internet cliches verging on parody. “My blood type is iced latte,” reads one post Looking at this well-curated online presence, you might well be convinced that Musera is, as they suggest, Manchester through and through

candidates.evidence_text: A public consultation has opened on changes that could affect who secures one of the sought-after grammar school's 204 Year 7 places Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Girls living close to Altrincham Grammar School for Girls could lose priority for places to children attending four designated primary schools under proposed changes to its admissions policy A public consultation has opened on plans to give pupils from four primary schools belonging to the same academy trust as AGGS priority over other applicants who have passed the entrance examination – even if they live closer to the school The proposals, which would take effect from September 2028, could have significant implications for Altrincham families whose daughters attend local primary schools outside Bright Futures Educational Trust Under the existing admissions system, girls who pass the entrance examination and live within the school's eight-mile catchment area are generally prioritised according to how close they live to AGGS, after higher-priority categories have been considered But the proposed arrangements would introduce a new category giving preference to qualifying pupils attending four primary schools within Bright Futures Educational Trust

candidates.evidence_text: The report also proposes charges at Thorley Lane car park in Timperley, which is currently free Share on WhatsApp Share via Email The report proposes charges at Thorley Lane car park in Timperley, which is currently free Motorists in Altrincham could face parking charges until 8pm and on Sundays under new proposals put forward by Trafford Council The changes form part of the council's draft budget for 2027/28, which aims to raise an additional £250,000 a year from parking charges across the borough The proposals include extending on-street charging hours in Altrincham, Sale and parts of Stretford, alongside revised tariffs for council-owned car parks, the introduction of Sunday charging and extended charging hours from 8am to 8pm In Altrincham, council-operated car parks include Regent Road and Oakfield Road, while nearby council car parks include Cecil Road, Victoria Road and Brown Street in Hale, and Balmoral Road and Baker Street in Timperley Currently, charges at these car parks generally apply between 8am and 6pm, Monday to Saturday, with parking free on Sundays

candidates.evidence_text: A man accused of killing a head teacher by driving for more than a mile with the victim trapped under his car was tackled to the ground by a police officer the next day Simon Richardson, 35, was arrested on 21 April, the day after his black Volvo XC90 crashed into 56-year-old Michael Mullins at a junction in Warburton, Trafford Mullins, who had been cycling home from Stretford Grammar School, was dragged at speeds of over 60mph (97km/h) before he finally came loose on a country lane in Lymm, Cheshire, where he died a short time later Richardson, who denies murder and manslaughter, has also pleaded not guilty to dangerous driving and is on trial at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court The jury of six men and six women were told Richardson, of no fixed address but from the Sale area, swapped the Volvo for a silver Ford transit van on the evening of the collision The Volvo itself was stopped shortly after 19:30 BST at an Asda petrol station in Altrincham having been spotted by officers

candidates.evidence_text: The Environment, Food and Rural Affairs Committee said firefighting aircraft, disposable barbecue restrictions and a public awareness campaign were needed to tackle rising wildfire risk The report follows this year's severe wildfire season, including fires that prompted military deployment in south Wales, destroyed 19 homes in Stourbridge and scorched land in the Cairngorms, Staffordshire and Suffolk The government said improving wildfire preparedness was a "major priority" A report by the cross-party committee said fires could no longer be regarded as rare or exceptional events, warning that climate change was increasing both their frequency and severity It said wildfire should now be treated as part of the UK's long-term climate resilience challenge, with better preparation needed for future fire seasons Fire and rescue services in England and Wales responded to 1,132 wildfires between 1 January and 16 August, more than the total number recorded during the whole of 2025

candidates.evidence_text: From the fabulous Feast of Fire celebrations to the iconic Christmas Lights Switch-On, the town centre will host an exciting calendar of entertainment as the Greater Manchester Town of Culture 2026 The programme will showcase the very best of Oldham's culture, creativity and community spirit with a series of free family-friendly events The programme begins with the Feast of Fire event on Saturday 31 October 2026. A joint celebration of Halloween and Bonfire Night, this spellbinding event will light up the heart of the town centre with fire dance performances and The Lips Halloween Show by Puppets with Guts foll Then, just two weeks later, the festive season will officially begin with the Oldham Christmas Lights Switch-On event on Saturday 14 November, starting from 1pm. The day will feature meet and greets with Peppa Pig, appearances from Oldham's mascots and activities by the Spindles The celebrations will continue into the evening with the big Switch On Show from 5.30pm featuring Father Christmas, Peppa Pig's Dance Party, Oldham Rock Choir and performances from Fierce Dance The Mayor of Oldham Cllr Pam Byrne will also take part in the celebrations before a local school child competition winner will switch on the town's Christmas lights. candidates.evidence_text: Experience Bolton’s FREE winter light art festival and enjoy four unforgettable nights of spectacular illuminated installations, captivating performances, and immersive experiences for all ages Curated in partnership by Bolton Council and Things That Go On Things, Put Big Light On Festival will run from Thursday 19 November to Sunday 22 November across Bolton town centre, between 5pm and 9pm every day With illuminated installations, roaming performers, and larger-than-life creations, the festival will showcase a mix of contemporary outdoor arts and family-friendly performances designed to surprise and delight audiences At the heart of this year’s festival, the Loom of Light by dbnAudile will take inspiration from Bolton’s textile heritage to transform Victoria Square into a mesmerising and striking walk-through artwork Using illuminated threads of light and colour to create an evolving structure that visitors can explore from within, this showstopping and interactive feature offers a contemporary interpretation of the weaving traditions that helped shape the town’s textile history Stretching across the square, the installation promises a memorable visual experience, with glowing strands of light creating a dramatic backdrop for photographs, exploration, and discovery throughout the festival

candidates.evidence_text: Wigan Council is introducing new orders to tackle anti-social behaviour in Wigan and Leigh town centres, including targeted powers against e-bikes and scooters These Public Space Protection Orders (PSPOs) will be in place for three years to support the police, council and other authorities in tackling a wide range of issues, reduce crime and help people feel safer in their communities This introduction follows an extensive review of previous orders and a public consultation held over the summer which gathered significant feedback from residents, businesses and the community sector Councillor Kevin Anderson, cabinet portfolio holder for Police, Crime and Civil Contingencies, said: “Residents, businesses and visitors all took part in our consultation, and it was clear that anti-social behaviour remains a concern “Most people who visit, live and work in our town centres do so responsibly, and these orders are aimed at addressing the small number of behaviours that negatively impact our communities, while ensuring support remains available for those who may be vulnerable.” The orders prohibit several anti-social behaviours, with new powers to enforce against anti-social use of cycles, e-bikes and scooters, and drug-related litter and paraphernalia

candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei . Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. Together, they paint a picture of globalisation.. Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. The exhibition also features the world premiere of a new body of work created especially for the vast spaces of the Warehouse – Eight-Nation Alliance Flags made from millions of buttons, as well as a new version of History Of Bombs made entirely from toy bricks.. The new commissions sit alongside large-scale works by the artist which are going on show in the UK for the first time: Law of the Journey (2017), a 47m long inflatable migrant boat containing hundreds of human figures and the artist’s largest artwork to date; Wang Family Ancestral Hall (2015), a Ming dynasty ancestral temple reassembled from 1,500 individual wooden pieces ; and La Commedia Umana (2017-21), a black Murano glass chandelier made up of over 2,000 pieces and weighing nearly 3 tonnes. Also on show is Circle of Animals/Zodiac Heads (2010), a re-envisioning of the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac.. Button Up! immerses visitors in Ai Weiwei’s fearless interrogation of the forces past and present that drive today’s injustices – while championing art’s enduring power to challenge and inspire.. . . . “I’m not interested in making very big things just for the sake of it. But in Manchester, that wonderful Warehouse space calls for monumental work. Visiting the city for this exhibition – the birthplace of the Industrial Revolution – and reflecting on Britain’s global territorial expansion made me realise I had to explore that history and understand how it connects to the forces driving today’s wars and global crises. The world today is deeply divided, with tragedy all around. Understanding history goes hand in hand with standing up for truth and justice.”. Ai Weiwei. . . Explore. . Ai Weiwei | Dream Space . The untold story of the rebellious middle child of Emmeline Pankhurst takes centre stage in this irresistible hip hop, funk and soul musical that moves your feet and fires your spirit. Whilst her mother and sister battled for women's suffrage, Sylvia ignited a revolution for the forgotten: working women, the impoverished, the silenced. Caught between her family and her beliefs, Sylvia risked it all to bring change to millions. With an electrifying score by Josh Cohen and DJ Walde , renowned choreographer and storyteller Kate Prince (ZooNation - Message in a Bottle, Some Like it Hip Hop, Into the Hoods, The Mad Hatter’s Tea Party ) delivers her Olivier-nominated vision in this theatrical treat that audiences can’t get enough of. Starring powerhouse talent Beverley Knight , ( Sister Act, The Drifters Girl, Memphis the Musical ) in a show stopping performance as Emmeline Pankhurst, this is your chance see her in a career defining turn that won her the Olivier Award for Best Actress in a Supporting Role. Naomi Katiyo ( Hamilton, Just For One Day: The Live Aid Musical ) stars as Sylvia Pankhurst, a role that brings depth, heart, and fire to the stage. Direct from London’s Old Vic theatre where it played to sold out houses and instant standing ovations, SYLVIA is more than a musical – it's a manifesto set to music, a revolution you can dance to, a story that roars and shakes the rafters. Book now. You don’t want to miss this. Olivier Award Win for Best Actress in a Supporting Role Olivier Nominated for Best New Musical and Best Theatre Choreographer. candidates.lead: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians.
candidates.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

candidates.evidence_text: We’re inviting young people to explore music for film and compose their own soundtrack this summer! Whether your child already attends our Saturday Music Club, or just wants to try something new, our Young Musician’s Summer School is suitable for all abilities! Across this 5 day course, we’ll be exploring music for film, and working on composing music for the silent film ‘A Trip to the Moon’. The course will conclude with a live performance soundtracking the film for family and friends. We welcome all abilities and instruments to take part in this course. You can bring your own instruments, but we have keyboards, guitars, bass, violins, drums and percussion on site which can be used if you don’t have an instrument. Please email learning@bandonthewall.org if you have any questions about this course

candidates.evidence_text: The Olllam is a band that fuses Irish traditional music with the modern jazz/post-rock energy of Detroit. Led by uilleann piper John McSherry, the band features Joe Dart (Vulfpeck), Michael Shimmin, Ross Ainslie, Seán O’Meara, and Joe Hettinga. Following their acclaimed album elllegy (RTÉ Radio 1 Best Group), The Olllam has collaborated with GRAMMY-nominated producer Zedd, shared the stage in Belfast with actor Anthony Boyle (Netflix’s House of Guinness), and recently completed a landmark U.S. tour in November 2025. From ancient airs to future soundscapes, The Olllam is not just carrying the tradition forward—they’re reinventing it

The opening marks Open Restaurant Group’s 9th restaurant to date and its second site in Greater Manchester, following the launch of Arcadian in Di At the heart of the restaurant will be a four-to-five-seat chef’s counter, placing guests directly at the pass for an up-close view of the kitchen in action. At Counter, he challenges convention by exploring what British cooking can The menu puts this philosophy into practice with dishes that combine unexpected ingredients and inventive flavour pairings. Highlights include the Beef Tartare Pressed Croissant, pairing aged beef with a crispy pressed croissant, smoked oyster mayo, wasabi and pickled shallot; th From the grill, guests can expect the Satay Spatchcock Chicken, served with peanut satay, fermented chilli, coconut, burnt lime and crispy shallo t, alongside Turbot Steak, a bone-in cut finished with brown butter, green chilli and preserved lemon

candidates.evidence_text: It’s been a busy week at Labour Party Conference in Liverpool, with technology, growth and devolution featuring heavily in many of the conversations we’ve been part of In his first Conference speech as Prime Minister, Andy Burnham talked about devolving more power to places, backing businesses to grow and taking some of what has worked in Greater Manchester into a wider national approach. He also confirmed that AI will be a central focus of the That felt particularly relevant following an event we hosted through the UK Tech Cluster Group with AI Minister Kanishka Narayan, North East Mayor Kim McGuinness and other regional leaders, looking at AI, devolution and local growth One of the clearest themes from the discussion was that devolution should not mean every place trying to build the same thing. Different regions have different strengths, assets and specialisms, and there was a strong view that greater collaboration between places could create bi Procurement and buying local also featured strongly. The discussion highlighted the role public sector buying power can play in supporting regional businesses, helping successful pilots move into commercial contracts and strengthening UK capability in areas such as AI and cyber There was also a broader conversation about sovereignty and the UK’s role internationally. The discussion was not about trying to own every part of the AI stack, but about understanding where the UK already has genuine capability and where it makes sense to build more. Strengths

Different regions have different strengths, assets and specialisms, and there was a strong view that greater collaboration between places could create bi Procurement and buying local also featured strongly. The discussion highlighted the role public sector buying power can play in supporting regional businesses, helping successful pilots move into commercial contracts and strengthening UK capability in areas such as AI and cyber There was also a broader conversation about sovereignty and the UK’s role internationally. The discussion was not about trying to own every part of the AI stack, but about understanding where the UK already has genuine capability and where it makes sense to build more. Strengths

candidates.lead: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing.
candidates.evidence_text: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing. As investors grow increasingly selective, the capital ecosystem has become polarised. More capital is being concentrated in fewer companies while the market for exits remains difficult Financial news recently added another dimension to that discussion. AI-related shares fell last week after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for a slower approach to the development of increasingly capable AI models. Nvidia finished the day down 3.4%, SoftBank fell 10.7% in Tokyo Additionally, the Bank of England is predicted to increase interest rates later this year, which could affect the North West's tech funding landscape by raising the cost of capital across the board, compressing valuations, pushing investors toward profitability over growth-at-all The British Business Bank's 2026 Small Business Equity Tracker found that equity investment into UK smaller businesses fell 4% to £12.3bn in 2025. Seed deal numbers fell 27% and venture deals fell 13%. AI companies attracted 44% of all investment into smaller businesses while the Beauhurst recorded £14.4bn of UK equity investment across 2,799 deals in the first half of 2026 but three AI companies accounted for 29% of all the capital raised. Those very large rounds can make the overall market look stronger than it feels to businesses raising at seed or Ser Beauhurst's analysis shows that UK equity investment more than doubled between 2017 and 2021 to £32.2bn while annual exits remained at around 400 to 500. An exit takes a median of four years from a funding round

candidates.evidence_text: A moonlit community run which aims to empower women and girls to stay active and enjoy outdoor exercise through the winter months comes to Platt Fields Park this week Organised by Manchester Parks in partnership with the running community, the welcoming and inclusive event is not just for experienced runners but for people just getting started and who are looking to become more active, helping them connect with local walking or running groups The event offers a chance to meet local run clubs, find new running partners and pick up tips to run safely through the darker months. Taking place on Thu 22 Oct from 6pm-9pm, the event is open to all genders and abilities, but organisers hope that it will be particularly helpful The first event earlier this year saw 210 people take part to complete a 3k run or walk around the park in a series of waves. Some of the more experienced runners even completed all seven waves and bagged themselves a half marathon The format will be similar this month, with guided runs led by local clubs with several running/jogging waves of a 3k route around the park. It follows the launch of Sheridan’s open-fire concept Arcadian in Didsbury last month The 60-cover restaurant will open in the Island Building on John Dalton Street. Highlights include the Beef Tartare Pressed Croissant, pairing aged beef with a crispy pressed croissant, smoked oyster mayo, wasabi and pickled shallot; th From the grill, guests can expect the Satay Spatchcock Chicken, served with peanut satay, fermented chilli, coconut, burnt lime and crispy shallot, alongside Turbot Steak, a bone-in cut finished with brown butter, green chilli and preserved lemon

Also look With prices ranging from affordable handmade gifts to collector-quality pieces, there’s something for every budget. And every exhibitor is selected by an independent panel of craft experts, so you can be sure to find quality pieces demonstrating originality and craftsmanship. Fro Alongside browsing and buying, visitors can enjoy an inspiring programme of talks, live demonstrations and hands-on workshops featuring exciting names from the worlds of craft, design and food. Highlights include free drop-in animation workshops using clay, food and other materia “GNCCF offers a connection you simply can’t get online or on the high street – the chance to meet the makers, hear the stories behind the work and invest in beautifully made pieces that will be cherished for years to come.”

This guided walking tour will bring those stories to life. Led by a local expert, the experience is set to be a lively introduction to the people, places and ideas that have shaped one of the UK’s most influential cities The tour will begin at Manchester Central Library, that impossible to miss, grand circular landmark on St Peter’s Square. The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

candidates.lead: Bolton Car Boot Sale at Bolton Car Boot Sale
candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. Cesc Fabregas will take on United as a manager for the first time, more than two decades on from his most infamous run-in with the club as a player Fabregas was a teenager on the Gunners' bench in October 2004 when Arsene Wenger's side travelled to Old Trafford chasing a 50th unbeaten match in the Premier League . The game would go on to be better known for what happened after the final whistle, though, with home manager Sir The encounter would come to be known as 'Pizzagate', with mystery surrounding who threw the food in question. A few years on, speculation began to mount that Fabregas might have been involved, though he initially kept his mouth shut Fabregas was identified as a likely suspect by Ferguson himself, while former Arsenal centre-back Martin Keown stoked the fire further. evidence_packet.evidence_text: For the second year running, our friends from the AI Café are back to make sure you leave the festival with more questions than you arrived with. Their plan is simple: to excite you, astound you and make you take stock of just how quickly this field is moving Expect a relaxed, afternoon of conversations about artificial intelligence, its ethics, the future of work and what might come next, alongside talks from people working at the cutting edge of AI If you're a technologist, business leader, students or just curious about AI, this is for you. No expert knowledge required 📅 Date: Friday 12th February 2027 🕒 Time: 15:30-17:00 📍 Location: TBC 🎟️ Tickets: £10 (Early Bird) £15 (Standard) Free (Manchester Digital Members) Manchester Digital members - check your recent emails or speak to your membership manager for your free discount code This event is part of the Manchester Digital Festival 2027, a week long event bringing together the businesses, talent and leadership powering Greater Manchester's tech sector.
